_policy: Every consciously deferred piece of work gets a row: what was deferred, why, what enforcement exists meanwhile, and a review-by date. `cargo xtask deferrals --check` (weekly scheduled CI) fails once a row passes its date un-re-decided — a deferral nobody re-examines is a silent forever. Re-deciding means either building the thing (delete the row) or re-dating it with a fresh reason in the same commit. Decisions intended to be permanent do not belong here; they get ADRs.

deferrals.what: Three of the pinned suite's 22 auth/* client scenarios as host-SUT gates. Re-decided 2026-11-20: the other 19 are built and gated. The reference host has an OAuth mode (`--oauth-conformance`, crate feature `oauth`, in neither `default` nor `cli`) on rmcp 3.9.0's `auth` feature — discovery, registration (pre-registered, Client ID Metadata Document, dynamic), PKCE S256, `state`, the RFC 8707 `resource`, scope selection, step-up and client_credentials are rmcp's; the host adds the reaction to 401/403, a three-request authorization budget and a headless consent step that refuses any authorization endpoint that is not loopback. `cargo xtask conformance` runs 20 scenarios (suite.rs `AUTH_CLIENT_SCENARIOS`) after checking the suite's `list` against that set plus the not-run set: 19 pass, and auth/2025-03-26-oauth-metadata-backcompat is run as an expected failure (conformance/expected-failures.yaml). What remains: (1) auth/2025-03-26-oauth-metadata-backcompat failing; (2) auth/client-credentials-jwt [extension] not run; (3) auth/cross-app-access-complete-flow [extension] not run. Earlier history of this row: review item 2.8 (2026-10-13) entered the authorization pages into the registry (AUTH-001..AUTH-085 at 2025-11-25, AUTH-086..AUTH-194 at 2026-07-28) and judges the server's 401/403 challenge from a recording; that half is unchanged
deferrals.why: (1) is not ours to fix: the scenario's root authorization-server metadata carries issuer `<origin>/oauth`, which RFC 8414 section 3.3 says must not be used, and rmcp enforces that with no switch; working around a mix-up defence for a 2025-03-26 back-compat fixture would be the wrong trade. (2) needs rmcp's `auth-client-credentials-jwt`, which brings jsonwebtoken and the aws-lc-rs C library (licences outside deny.toml's allowlist, a C toolchain to build) into the tree for one extension scenario. (3) needs glue around rmcp's `auth-enterprise-managed` (RFC 8693 token exchange at the IdP, then a JWT-bearer grant) that has not been written; no new crate is involved, so it is the cheapest of the three to close. The trace validator still cannot use any of this: the flow runs between the client and the authorization server, off the MCP endpoint a recording captures (registry exclusions AUTH-* say clause by clause why)
deferrals.meanwhile: The gate runs the 20 on every `cargo xtask conformance`; a suite that adds, renames or drops an auth scenario fails the list check; the expected-failure entry goes stale loudly the day the backcompat scenario passes. `mcp-conformance test --client-command` keeps its four protocol scenarios as the default, so a client without OAuth is not failed on a feature it never claimed (and through the recording relay a spec-following client refuses the resource mismatch anyway — measured 2026-11-20). The AUTH-* registry entries judge the HTTP-observable challenge clauses on every recorded session; TRAN-009 and TRAN-054 stay excluded and point at them

deferrals.what: The STABLE suite pin only — xtask's SUITE_VERSION (0.1.16, the 2025-11-25 gate) — bumps when a stable 0.2.0 exists, refreshing both expected-failures baselines and the agreement divergence ledger in the same change. The draft ratchet DRAFT_SUITE_VERSION is not deferred: it tracks the alpha dist-tag (0.2.0-alpha.12 since 2026-10-01). 03-conformance-strategy states the two pins' separate triggers
deferrals.why: Re-decided 2026-10-12, the review-by (2026-10-15) being due: there is still nothing stable to bump to. npm `latest` is 0.1.16, published 2026-03-30 and unchanged for six and a half months; `alpha` is 0.2.0-alpha.12 (2026-10-01). Re-fetched 2026-10-12 (register 2.4). Pin bumps are deliberate PRs with a scenario diff review (03-conformance-strategy §Official-suite version policy)
deferrals.meanwhile: The watch is a gate, not a date: `cargo xtask suite-currency` (weekly, in `claims-expire`) fails the moment npm's `latest` stops being 0.1.16, and a red weekly run files a tracking issue. The weekly suite-alpha job runs the alpha dist-tag non-blocking; the draft ratchet pins alpha.12 and gates every check's status; conformance#338's fix arrives with the stable bump and its agreement-divergence entry will go stale loudly

deferrals.what: The MCP Apps extension (modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps, the site's `extensions/apps/*`) as an extension registry beside 2026-07-28, the way ADR-0023 entered tasks and skills: every MUST- and SHOULD-family keyword of its specification entered, the clauses a recording can show judged with corpus pairs, the rest excluded with reasons
deferrals.why: Review item 2.6 named tasks and skills, the two extensions the official suite and SEP-1730 single out; Apps is the third official extension and was not read for this change. Most of it binds the view-to-host bridge, which runs over postMessage inside the host and never reaches an MCP recording, but its server half — `ui://` resources and the tool metadata that points at them — does cross the MCP connection, so it cannot be excluded wholesale without reading its clauses, and an unread page is not an exclusion
deferrals.meanwhile: `extensions/apps/overview` and `extensions/apps/build` sit in `site_out_of_scope` of registry/2026-07-28/extensions/sources.json naming this row, so the weekly spec-drift run keeps them decided rather than silent; the official suite runs no Apps scenario either (0.2.0-alpha.12, read 2026-10-13)

deferrals.what: Removing chrono from the dependency tree, or the `deny.toml` ignore entry for RUSTSEC-2026-0543 ("chrono is unmaintained", informational, every version affected, no patched release)
deferrals.why: Entered 2026-11-19. chrono 0.4.45 is in Cargo.lock only as a dependency of rmcp (`cargo tree -i chrono`, at rmcp 3.9.0), which the everything server and the reference host are built on; nothing in this workspace calls it. rmcp 3.11.0, the newest release that day, still requires it, so there is no version of our own dependencies to move to, and replacing rmcp is not on the table (ADR-0009)
deferrals.meanwhile: `cargo deny` ignores exactly this advisory id, with the reason beside it in deny.toml; every other advisory still fails the build, including a real vulnerability in chrono, which would carry its own id. The validator, the recorder and `mcp-conformance` do not link rmcp outside their tests
